title: Gold Mine Collapse Near Al-Nuhud, RSF-Held West Kordofan, Kills At Least 67
detail: A cascading collapse of hand-dug shafts at the Al-Zaraa artisanal gold mine near Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan — territory held by the Rapid Support Forces — killed at least 67 people on September 16, 2026, according to the Sudanese Doctors Network, while an anonymous RSF source told AFP the toll was at least 82 dead and 50 wounded. Survivor Khair al-Sayyed Jabara said 'we don't know how many more are still inside,' and miner Amin Suleiman described how the shafts collapsed in sequence: 'each one pulled down those beside it.' Dozens of artisanal miners had been trapped since Tuesday morning; rescue teams lacked heavy machinery and relied on basic hand tools to dig through loose, sandy soil at depths of more than 30 meters, with no specialized rescue services present. The Sudanese Doctors Network denounced the absence of safety standards and protective or rescue equipment in RSF-administered mining zones, saying the conditions 'turn mining into a direct threat' to civilians. Gold remains one of Sudan's few functioning export sectors amid the war; fatal collapses at unregulated artisanal mines have recurred throughout the conflict.

title: UN Chief Guterres Calls for Accountability From Countries Fueling Sudan's War
detail: UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on September 16, 2026 that the situation in Sudan is 'absolutely horrible,' calling the humanitarian crisis 'devastating' and the suffering of the Sudanese people 'intolerable.' Guterres said the conflict 'is fueled by a number of countries from the outside' and that 'there should be accountability for the kind of interference in which some countries provide weapons to parties to a conflict when those weapons are used massively to attack civilians.' His remarks followed a UN fact-finding mission report earlier in September that found foreign weapons, military technology, fighters and logistical networks are sustaining Sudan's war and expanding both sides' ability to strike distant civilian areas with drones.
